notes.statement: The hotfire review dashboard silently showed three-day-old engine_test_runs data last week. The Propulsion stakeholder wants a 60-minute staleness check run before every review.
Manufacturing Quality wants a weekly SLA report on NCR table freshness, grouped by owner team. Datasets never measured must be reported as unknown, not fresh.
Three forward deployed engineers each hand-rolled their own freshness checks with different thresholds. The team wants one shared capability where thresholds are policy configuration, not code.
The BOM cost dashboard broke after an upstream column rename and nobody noticed for days. The request asks for schema-contract drift by field, which is a different check from time-based freshness.

The overlap report consolidates syn-req-001, syn-req-003 and syn-req-004 into one policy-configured dataset freshness monitor that reports fresh, stale or unknown grouped by owner team. This is the planning position recorded in the report; no stakeholder decided it.
syn-req-002 (schema drift) is excluded from the freshness capability and deferred to a separate plan. The reserved criterion id AC-SCHEMA-SUPPLY is not defined and must not be assumed.

The plan defines four executable acceptance criteria: AC-FRESH-PROPULSION (59, 61 and three-day fixtures against a 60-minute policy threshold), AC-SLA-QUALITY (multi-team NCR fixture with one never-measured dataset), AC-POLICY-FDE (threshold changed only in policy config, no hard-coded thresholds in source), and AC-CONTRACT (all emitted records validate against the pinned schema).

The unknown-not-fresh rule is carried into two criteria: AC-SLA-QUALITY forbids counting a never-measured dataset as fresh, and AC-CONTRACT requires that a record with last_update null always has status unknown.

contract/health-record version 1 is labelled SYNTHETIC in its description. It requires dataset_id, owner_team, checked_at, a freshness object (status, staleness_minutes, threshold_minutes) and a schema object (status, drift).

The AC-CONTRACT field list (dataset, owner_team, status, last_update, threshold, checked_at, schema version) does not match contract/health-record v1. The contract uses dataset_id, nests status and threshold under freshness, has no last_update field, and declares no schema-version property beyond the top-level version.
The AC-CONTRACT field list and the health-record contract are probably the same record under two naming schemes. This is an inference; reconciling them is needed before AC-CONTRACT can be verified.
The three hand-rolled FDE checks probably share logic with the checks behind syn-req-001 and syn-req-003 and could migrate onto the shared capability. No request states this.

Nine items are unresolved in the overlap report: timestamp source per dataset, whether every dataset has a timestamp, the NCR table list and owner-team source, the NCR threshold value, who owns and approves threshold policy, whether the 60-minute check is a hard gate or a warning, the delivery mode, the FDE thresholds and migration, and whether no-timestamp and never-checked both map to unknown. The syn-req-002 scope decision is also open.
The plan does not say whether a dataset whose staleness equals the threshold exactly (60 minutes) is fresh or stale. The criteria only cover 59 (fresh) and 61 (stale).

Candidate verification procedure: build fixtures per criterion (59, 61 and three-day engine_test_runs; a multi-team NCR set with one never-measured dataset; a schema set spanning fresh, stale and unknown), run the check and compare statuses and record fields, then change only the policy threshold and re-run to confirm the status flips.
